message.content: {"0": {"original": "Wikipedia will go offline for 24 hours to protest U.S. anti-piracy laws, with 59", "rephrased": "The English version of the online encyclopedia Wikipedia plans to shut down for 24 hours to protest proposed U.S. anti-piracy legislation, a move supported by a majority of its user base who favor a global blackout over a limited U.S.-only action.", "summary": "Wikipedia plans a 24-hour global shutdown to protest U.S. anti-piracy laws."}, "1": {"original": "A number of other websites are also taking part, including the social media site", "rephrased": "Beyond Wikipedia, various digital platforms including the social media site Reddit, the Boing Boing blog, and sites owned by the Cheezburger Network are participating in the coordinated online protest against the proposed U.S. anti-piracy laws.", "summary": "Multiple digital platforms are joining the protest against U.S. anti-piracy laws."}, "2": {"original": "Supporters claim the laws pose an existential threat, while opponents argue the", "rephrased": "Proponents of the protest argue that the proposed U.S. anti-piracy laws pose an existential threat to the online encyclopedia, whereas critics contend that the planned shutdown undermines the site's reputation for political neutrality and risks alienating the public.", "summary": "Protest supporters view the laws as an existential threat, while critics fear the action harms Wikipedia's neutrality."}, "3": {"original": "Wales urged students to finish homework early to avoid access issues, hoping the", "rephrased": "The co-founder of the online encyclopedia advised students to complete their homework early to avoid access disruptions, while expressing hope that the protest would overwhelm Washington's phone systems and arguing that the proposed legislation is poorly written and overbroad.", "summary": "Wikipedia's co-founder urges preparation for the shutdown and criticizes the proposed laws as overbroad."}}
